To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the linguistic encoding and decoding of affective information can be described as the linguistic encoding of deviation, augmentation, and duplication.

the linguistic encoding and processing of affective color is based on the following three principles: (a) unexpectedness is encoded linguistically by deviations in the build of the language; (b) deviations are of two types, space-based and symbol-based; (c) space-based deviations are manifested by the omission of a linguistic form or pattern, and the omission is compensated for by the addition of an extra form; symbol-based deviations are manifested in two ways, augmentation and duplication.
the linguistic build of Dutch encodes affective color by deviations, augmentations, and duplications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the linguistic packaging of unexpectedness and the affective consequences thereof.
the linguistic packaging of affective information in the build of Dutch.
the question of how language encodes affect, and how affect is encoded in language.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the language system is not an isolated system.
the linguistic encoding and processing of affective information is a complex and intricate affair, which involves a variety of linguistic devices.
the linguistic build of Dutch encodes affective color by means of deviations, augmentations, and duplications of symbols.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the build of language provides a number of linguistic mechanisms for indexing affective information.
unexpectedness is a key to understanding the linguistic encoding of emotion.
unexpectedness of information is a key factor in the build of Dutch.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the linguistic encoding and representation of affective information is a complex phenomenon, and that it is not limited to a few well-studied cases such as the case of intensification.
the linguistic encoding (and decoding) of affect is not limited to lexical items.
affect can be induced by the build of language.
